To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Handover for Inês: border revenues launch, Thursday 26 November

Inês,

I am so sorry to leave you with this, especially this late. My father is ill, and I am with my family. I do not know how long I will be away, so Thursday’s launch is yours.

Before the practical list: I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. You do not need to wait for answers from me or act as though you are only standing in. Please make the decisions you think are right.

The order in which I would do things:

1. Correct the slides and make PDF v7 the only source for numbers

I found the figure 3 error this afternoon. Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, without the free-allocation phase-out applied.

The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number obviously does.

PDF v7 on the drive is corrected, including pages 3, 14 and 15. Deck v4 is not: slides 6 and 9 still need changing. Slide 9 is the revenue chart. Please also search the deck and speaker notes for any remaining “2.1”, so we do not correct the visible chart and leave the old number somewhere else. Use PDF v7 as the reference throughout.

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, please say so plainly. Do not take responsibility for it or feel you need to protect me.

2. Get the embargoed press release replaced

Hanna sent the release to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday afternoon. It still says EUR 2.1 billion. The embargo lifts at 10:00 CET on Thursday 26 November, so this is the most time-sensitive item after the slides.

Please speak to Hanna first thing on Tuesday and ask her to:

- prepare a corrected release using PDF v7, including the headline and any summary wording or quotes that use the old number;
- send it to the same 34 contacts, clearly replacing the earlier version and withdrawing the EUR 2.1 billion figure;
- confirm to you that this has been done, rather than our simply assuming that everyone will notice a correction.

Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name or sign-off for the corrected release, she can go to him. You do not need to chase me for that.

Before 10:00 on Thursday, please check with Hanna that the corrected version is the one journalists have and that nothing goes out automatically with the old number.

3. Confirm the press calls and move them to you

Two journalists asked Hanna for background calls before the event: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar currently has Wednesday 25 November at 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each, with Hanna to confirm.

Please ask Hanna to put the calls in your name and confirm the arrangements with both journalists. Use EUR 1.4 billion from the outset. If either time genuinely does not work, ask Hanna to reschedule rather than leaving either journalist expecting a call from me.

For the correction itself, the simple line is: an earlier run was used in figure 3 and the summary; the corrected figure is EUR 1.4 billion; the analysis and conclusion are unchanged.

4. Confirm badges and the revised running order with Tomás

Tomás needs the final names of anyone attending from our side by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00 at the latest. Security will not admit people whose names he has not received. Please confirm who is actually coming and send him the list before that deadline. Do not leave Hanna’s or anyone else’s attendance assumed rather than confirmed.

Tomás will collect the badges. Guests need to be at the Parliament security entrance by 12:00. The event is in the Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office, and there is a light lunch outside the room from 12:00.

The MEP now has a vote and must leave at 13:30. Tomás has asked for a 15-minute presentation and a 12:50 panel start. The working run of show is therefore:

- 12:00 — guests at security; lunch outside the room
- 12:30 — welcome from Katarina Lindqvist, 5 minutes
- 12:35 — your presentation, 15 minutes
- 12:50 — panel with Dr Abena Owusu-Mensah, Florian Kessler and you; Lindqvist moderating
- Before 13:30 — Lindqvist wants to take at least two questions herself
- 13:30 — Lindqvist leaves
- Afterwards — remaining discussion/Q&A, with a view to closing at 14:00

Please agree the last part with Tomás in advance. In particular, decide who moderates after Lindqvist leaves and who closes the event. Her request for questions also means we cannot simply leave all audience questions until the original 13:40 Q&A slot. It would be better to bring them into the discussion while she is still there, if Tomás agrees.

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invitation. She tested it and it works. Please do one final check that she has the revised timings, since she is joining remotely from Accra.

5. On the panel, do not let Kessler make the whole event about the 80%

Kessler has told us that AESU will raise both pass-through and resource shuffling. His members’ concern is especially about small manufacturers, for whom they say pass-through is lower.

The response on pass-through is straightforward: 80% is our central case, not the only case we examined. Annex B tests 60% and 40%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly and do not get defensive. You ran those runs yourself, so you are on extremely solid ground here.

He will try to make the 80% assumption the story of the launch. Acknowledge the disagreement, explain the sensitivity results, and then bring the discussion back to the paper as a whole and the LDC questions we are there to discuss. Do not let him set the tone or turn the entire panel into a yes/no argument about one assumption.

On resource shuffling, we agree that it is a risk. That is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. There is no need to pretend we have solved every possible implementation problem.

Abena will probably support us on the LDC side; she was very strong on the call. Give her room to make those points herself rather than answering everything for her.

6. After the event

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is attending with a colleague. For their grant report, she needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange for someone to take a couple of usable photos and make sure we keep a reliable attendance count. Those can go to Lucy after the launch; they are not something to worry about on Thursday morning.

Finally: you can call me, but after 09:00 tomorrow I may not pick up. If I do not answer, leave me a message and make the call yourself. I would much rather you do that than have something wait on me.

I am sorry that you are inheriting both my absence and my mistake. But I am not worried about whether you can do this. In Lisbon, at the COP side event, the projector died and you rescued my panel. You were calm, clear and completely in command of the room. You are better live than you think, and you do not need slides or me beside you to be good at this.

Thank you, Inês. I am very grateful it is you.

Marieke
